messages:
alex: CI red on master — session_resume_test failing intermittently on linux-amd64. Seen ~1/10 runs. Can someone take a quick look?

ci-bot: flake detector triggered for job: runtime-integration-linux-amd64 (build/7890). Recommend rerun with artifacts preserved.

sana: thanks for the heads up. pinging @jamie who owns the session resume area.

jamie: on it. can you paste the failing log + the exact test cmd/env? sounds like a timing window in reconnect.

alex: paste: ```
--- FAIL: TestSessionResume (0.45s)
    session_resume_test.go:112: expected session.state.userID == "u123" got ""
    runtime.go:234: reconnect handler returned nil state
    goroutine 23 [running]:
    ...
```
Env: GOMAXPROCS=2, go test ./serve -run TestSessionResume -race

jamie: thanks. please try locally with GOMAXPROCS=1 and -race off, also run with TEST_SEED=42 to see if seed affects it:
```bash
TEST_SEED=42 GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./serve -run TestSessionResume -v
```
The reconnect path uses a non-deterministic timer; lowering procs sometimes exposes races.

alex: re-ran locally 20x with those settings, failed once. I also tried TEST_SEED=7 and it passed.

sana: I kicked a CI rerun with preserved artifacts + added --repeat=50 (job 7890-rerun). Link: <ci/retry/7890-rerun>

ops-oncall: quick note — if this keeps flaking, please bisect to narrow to commit range and mark as high-priority for the release branch. Also avoid adding sleeps; prefer knobs or hooks.

jamie: plan: I'll spin up a reproducer that forces reconnect ordering (inject a sync point) and run under heavy scheduling jitter (stress-ng in a container). If repro, will add a deterministic synchonization hook in the test to remove the timing dependence, or make the code robust to missing state during transient reconnects.

alex: FYI I opened a draft PR with an assert-change that surfaces the issue faster: #PR1234 (not merging yet).

sana: perfect. please post results here once you get a stable repro or a bisect. :thumbsup:

jamie: will do. if anyone else sees a repro on CI, drop the job id here and I'll correlate artifacts.
